test_7592|a|Phase transition - induced elasticity of alpha - helical bioelastomeric fibres and networks .

test_7593|t|
test_7593|a|Natural elastomeric fibres play central structural and functional roles in a variety of tissues produced by many organisms from diverse Phyla .

test_7594|t|
test_7594|a|Most of these fibres feature amorphous structure and their long - range elastic response is well described within the framework of entropic ( rubber - like ) elasticity .

test_7595|t|
test_7595|a|Recently , it has been recognized that long - range reversible deformation can also occur in biomacromolecular fibres or networks that feature significant secondary structure and long - range order .

test_7596|t|
test_7596|a|Their elastomeric response is then associated with conformational changes of the backbone of the constitutive protein - based polymers .

test_7597|t|
test_7597|a|Under axially imposed loads , several groups of proteins whose structure is dominated by alpha - helical coiled - coil structures can undergo unfolding transitions and secondary structure transformations , for example from coiled - coil alpha - helices to beta - sheet strands .

test_7598|t|
test_7598|a|In contrast to rubber - like biopolymers , the retractive elastic force in these biomacromolecular materials is not dominated by a return to a maximum entropic state , but is mostly the result of variations in internal energy associated with the conformational changes .

test_7599|t|
test_7599|a|Here , a review of alpha - helix based elastomeric materials is presented that encompasses examples and experimental evidence across multiple length scales , from the molecular to the macroscopic scale .

test_7600|t|
test_7600|a|We begin by summarizing the basic thermodynamic formalism of thermoelasticity .

test_7601|t|
test_7601|a|While this formalism is well established for amorphous ( entropically - dominated ) fibres under tensile loading , its extension towards conformational ( internal energy - dominated ) elasticity is less known .

test_7602|t|
test_7602|a|Recent experimental evidence as well as corroborating computer simulations are then reviewed and discussed in the light of secondary structure and nano - scale features of these biopolymers .

test_7603|t|
test_7603|a|Comparisons are also drawn with physiologically important structural fibres that share common characteristics at the molecular and the nano - scale , including intermediate filament ( IF ) proteins from the cell cytoskeleton , myosins from motor proteins , and fibrin from blood clot .

test_7604|t|
test_7604|a|We conclude with a discussion on future directions and opportunities for these materials from a biomimetics engineering perspective .

test_9773|t|
test_9773|a|A synchronous , concerted chemical process is rigorously divided by the reaction force F ( R ) , the negative gradient of V ( R ) , into " reactant " and " product " regions which are dominated by structural changes and an intervening " transition " region which is electronically intensive .

test_9774|t|

test_9790|a|Calculation of wave - functions with frozen orbitals in mixed quantum mechanics / molecular mechanics methods .

test_9791|a|II .

test_9793|t|
test_9793|a|The application of the local basis equation ( Ferenczy and Adams , J . Chem . Phys . 2009 , 130 , 134108 ) in mixed quantum mechanics / molecular mechanics ( QM / MM ) and quantum mechanics / quantum mechanics ( QM / QM ) methods is investigated .

test_9794|t|
test_9794|a|This equation is suitable to derive local basis nonorthogonal orbitals that minimize the energy of the system and it exhibits good convergence properties in a self - consistent field solution .

test_9795|t|
test_9795|a|These features make the equation appropriate to be used in mixed QM / MM and QM / QM methods to optimize orbitals in the field of frozen localized orbitals connecting the subsystems .

test_9796|t|
test_9796|a|Calculations performed for several properties in divers systems show that the method is robust with various choices of the frozen orbitals and frontier atom properties .

test_9797|t|
test_9797|a|With appropriate basis set assignment , it gives results equivalent with those of a related approach [ G . G . Ferenczy previous paper in this issue ] using the Huzinaga equation .

test_9798|t|
test_9798|a|Thus , the local basis equation can be used in mixed QM / MM methods with small size quantum subsystems to calculate properties in good agreement with reference Hartree - Fock - Roothaan results .

test_9799|t|

test_9800|t|
test_9800|a|Conversely , the deformation of the wave - function near to the boundary is observed without bond charges and this has a significant effect on deprotonation energies but a less pronounced effect when the total charge of the system is conserved .

test_9801|t|
test_9801|a|The local basis equation can also be used to define a two layer quantum system with nonorthogonal localized orbitals surrounding the central delocalized quantum subsystem .

test_12019|a|Medical aspects of bio - terrorism .

test_12020|t|
test_12020|a|INTRODUCTION : Bioterrorism is a terrorist action involving the intentional release or dissemination of a biological warfare agent ( BWA ) , which includes some bacteria , viruses , rickettsiae , fungi or biological toxins .

test_12021|t|
test_12021|a|BWA is a naturally occurring or human - modified form that may kill or incapacitate humans , animals or plants as an act of war or terrorism .

test_12022|t|
test_12022|a|BWA is a weapon of choice for mass destruction and terrorism , because of the incubation period , less effective amount than chemical warfare agents , easily distribution , odorless , colorless , difficult to detect , no need of specialized equipment for production and naturally distribution which can easily be obtained .

test_12023|t|
test_12023|a|BWA may be disseminating as an aerosol , spray , explosive device , and by food or water .

test_12024|t|
test_12024|a|CLASSIFICATION : Based on the risk for human health , BWAs have been prioritized into three categories of A , B and C .

test_12025|t|
test_12025|a|Category A includes microorganisms or toxins that easily spread , leading to intoxication with high death rates such as Anthrax , Botulism , Plague , Smallpox , Tularemia and Viral hemorrhagic fevers .

test_12026|t|
test_12026|a|Category B has lower toxicity with wider range , including Staphylococcal Entrotoxin type B ( SEB ) , Epsilon toxin of Clostridium perfringens , Ricin , Saxotoxins , Abrin and Trichothecene mycotoxins .
test_12026	177	190	Trichothecene	drug

test_12027|t|
test_12027|a|The C category includes emerging pathogens that could also be engineered for mass spread such as Hanta viruses , multidrug - resistant tuberculosis , Nipah virus , the tick - borne encephalitis viruses , hemorrhagic fever viruses and yellow fever .

test_12028|t|
test_12028|a|CLINICAL MANIFESTATIONS OF BIOTOXINS IN HUMAN : Clinical features and severity of intoxication depend on the agent and exposed dose , route of entry , individual variation and environmental factors .

test_12029|t|
test_12029|a|Onset of symptoms varies from 2 - 24 h in Ricin to 24 - 96 h in Botulism .

test_12030|t|
test_12030|a|Clinical manifestations also vary from irritation of the eyes , skin and mucus membranes in T ( 2 ) toxin to an acute flaccid paralysis of bilateral cranial nerve impairment of descending manner in botulism .

test_12031|t|
test_12031|a|Most of the pyrogenic toxins such as SEB produce the same signs and symptoms as toxic shock syndrome including a rapid drop in blood pressure , elevated temperature , and multiple organ failure .

test_12032|t|
test_12032|a|MANAGEMENT : There is no specific antidote or effective treatment for most of the biotoxins .

test_12033|t|
test_12033|a|The clinical management is thus more supportive and symptomatic .

test_12034|t|
test_12034|a|Fortunately vaccines are now available for most of BWA .

test_12035|t|
test_12035|a|Therefore , immunization of personnel at risk of exposure is recommended .

test_12036|t|
test_12036|a|CONCLUSION : Biotoxins are very wide and bioterrorism is a heath and security threat that may induce national and international problems .

test_12037|t|
test_12037|a|Therefore , the security authorities , health professional and even public should be aware of bioterrorism .

test_18037|a|Considering the impact drug - like properties have on the chance of success .

test_18038|t|
test_18038|a|Many definitions of ' drug - like ' compound properties have been published ; based on the analysis of simple molecular properties of successful drugs .

test_18039|t|
test_18039|a|These are typically presented as rules that define acceptable boundaries for these properties .

test_18040|t|
test_18040|a|When a compound does not ' fit ' within these boundaries then its properties differ from those of the majority of drugs , which could indicate a higher risk of poor pharmacokinetics or safety outcomes in vivo .

test_18041|t|

test_18042|t|
test_18042|a|Alternatively , compounds can be ranked according to their similarity to marketed drugs using a continuous measure of drug - likeness .

test_18043|t|
test_18043|a|However , being similar to known drugs does not necessarily mean that a compound is more likely to become a drug and we demonstrate how a new approach , employing Bayesian methods , can be used to compare a set of successful drugs with a set of non - drug compounds to identify those properties that give the greatest distinction between the two sets , and hence the greatest increase in the likelihood of a compound becoming a successful drug .

test_18044|t|

test_18045|a|Therefore , it might be more appropriate to consider specific guidelines for drug - likeness that are project specific .

test_20133|a|CNA goes beyond the mere identification of flexible and rigid regions in a biomacromolecule in that it ( I ) provides a refined modeling of thermal unfolding simulations that also considers the temperature - dependence of hydrophobic tethers , ( II ) allows performing rigidity analyses on ensembles of network topologies , either generated from structural ensembles or by using the concept of fuzzy noncovalent constraints , and ( III ) computes a set of global and local indices for quantifying biomacromolecular stability .

test_20134|t|
test_20134|a|This leads to more robust results from rigidity analyses and extends the application domain of rigidity analyses in that phase transition points ( " melting points " ) and unfolding nuclei ( " structural weak spots " ) are determined automatically .

test_20135|a|Furthermore , CNA robustly handles small - molecule ligands in general .

test_20136|t|
test_20136|a|Such advancements are important for applying rigidity analysis to data - driven protein engineering and for estimating the influence of ligand molecules on biomacromolecular stability .

test_20137|t|
test_20137|a|CNA maintains the efficiency of FIRST such that the analysis of a single protein structure takes a few seconds for systems of several hundred residues on a single core .

test_20138|t|

test_21931|a|Development and Regulation of Biosimilars : Current Status and Future Challenges .

test_21932|t|
test_21932|a|Biologic medicinal products developed via rDNA technology as recombinant protein - based medicines that have been in clinical use since the early 1980s as original biopharmaceuticals have greatly contributed to the therapy of severe metabolic and degenerative diseases .

test_21933|t|
test_21933|a|The recent expiration of the data protection or patents for most of them created opportunities for the development of copy versions of original biopharmaceuticals with similar biologic activity ( termed biosimilars ) .

test_21934|t|
test_21934|a|Production of these new products is expected to meet worldwide demand , promote market competition , maintain the incentives for innovation , and sustain the healthcare systems .

test_21935|t|
test_21935|a|The licencing of these products , however , relies on the experience gained with the original biopharmaceuticals .

test_21936|t|
test_21936|a|Critical issues related to this class of medicinal products include their terminology ( to avoid confusion with generics and non - innovator copy versions that have not been tested according to the biosimilar guidelines ) , manufacturing , and regulation .

test_21937|t|
test_21937|a|The European Union ( EU ) has been the first to establish a regulatory framework for marketing authorization application ( MAA ) and has named these products biosimilars , a term also recently adopted by the US FDA .

test_21938|t|
test_21938|a|Unlike the conventional , more common small molecular weight human medicines and chemical generics , protein - based medicines exhibit higher molecular weight , complexity in structure and function that can be affected by changes in the manufacturing process .

test_21939|t|
test_21939|a|Therefore , biosimilars represent a relatively heterogeneous class of medicinal products that make their regulation quite challenging .

test_21940|t|
test_21940|a|According to the current understanding in the EU , a biosimilar is a copy version of an already authorized biopharmaceutical ( or reference product ) with similar biologic activity , physicochemical characteristics , efficacy , and safety , based on a full comparability exercise at quality , preclinical and clinical level to ensure similar efficacy and safety .

test_21941|t|
test_21941|a|Guidance has been provided through several Committee for Medicinal Products for Human Use ( CHMP ) guidelines as well as individual scientific advice requested from the European Medicines Agency ( EMA ) by various companies for the development and regulation of biosimilars .

test_21942|t|
test_21942|a|This review is mainly focused on the current status of regulation of biosimilars in the EU as well as on future challenges lying ahead for the improvement of the requirements needed for the marketing authorization of biosimilars .

test_21943|t|
test_21943|a|Emphasis is given on the quality requirements concerning these medicinal products ( biologics ) .

test_22773|t|

test_23783|a|RNA global alignment in the joint sequence - structure space using elastic shape analysis .

test_23784|t|
test_23784|a|The functions of RNAs , like proteins , are determined by their structures , which , in turn , are determined by their sequences .

test_23785|t|
test_23785|a|Comparison / alignment of RNA molecules provides an effective means to predict their functions and understand their evolutionary relationships .

test_23786|t|
test_23786|a|For RNA sequence alignment , most methods developed for protein and DNA sequence alignment can be directly applied .

test_23787|t|
test_23787|a|RNA 3 - dimensional structure alignment , on the other hand , tends to be more difficult than protein structure alignment due to the lack of regular secondary structures as observed in proteins .

test_23788|t|
test_23788|a|Most of the existing RNA 3D structure alignment methods use only the backbone geometry and ignore the sequence information .

test_23789|t|
test_23789|a|Using both the sequence and backbone geometry information in RNA alignment may not only produce more accurate classification , but also deepen our understanding of the sequence - structure - function relationship of RNA molecules .

test_23790|t|
test_23790|a|In this study , we developed a new RNA alignment method based on elastic shape analysis ( ESA ) .

test_23791|t|
test_23791|a|ESA treats RNA structures as three dimensional curves with sequence information encoded on additional dimensions so that the alignment can be performed in the joint sequence - structure space .

test_23792|t|
test_23792|a|The similarity between two RNA molecules is quantified by a formal distance , geodesic distance .

test_23793|t|
test_23793|a|Based on ESA , a rigorous mathematical framework can be built for RNA structure comparison .

test_23794|t|
test_23794|a|Means and covariances of full structures can be defined and computed , and probability distributions on spaces of such structures can be constructed for a group of RNAs .

test_23795|t|
test_23795|a|Our method was further applied to predict functions of RNA molecules and showed superior performance compared with previous methods when tested on benchmark datasets .

test_23796|t|
test_23796|a|The programs are available at http : / / stat . fsu . edu / ~ jinfeng / ESA . html .

test_26259|a|Simulations of droplet coalescence in simple shear flow .

test_26260|t|
test_26260|a|Simulating droplet coalescence is challenging because small - scale ( tens of nanometers ) phenomena determine the behaviour of much larger ( micron - to millimetre - scale ) droplets .

test_26261|t|
test_26261|a|In general , liquid droplets colliding in a liquid medium coalesce when the capillary number is less than a critical value .

test_26262|t|
test_26262|a|We present simulations of droplet collisions and coalescence in simple shear flow using the free - energy binary - liquid lattice Boltzmann method .

test_26263|t|
test_26263|a|In previous simulations of low - speed collisions , droplets coalesced at unrealistically high capillary numbers .

test_26264|t|
test_26264|a|Simulations of non - coalescing droplets have not been reported , and therefore the critical capillary number for simulated collisions was unknown .

test_26265|t|
test_26265|a|By simulating droplets with radii up to 100 lattice nodes , we determine the critical capillary number for coalescence and quantify the effects of several numerical and geometric parameters .

test_26266|t|
test_26266|a|The simulations were performed with a well - resolved interface , a Reynolds number of one , and capillary numbers from 0 . 01 to 0 . 2 .

test_26267|t|
test_26267|a|The ratio of the droplet radius and interface thickness has the greatest effect on the critical capillary number .

test_26268|t|
test_26268|a|As in experiments , the critical capillary number decreases with increasing droplet size .

test_26269|t|
test_26269|a|A second numerical parameter , the interface diffusivity ( Peclet number ) also influences the conditions for coalescence : coalescence occurs at higher capillary numbers with lower Peclet numbers ( higher diffusivity ) .

test_26270|t|
test_26270|a|The effects of the vertical offset between the droplets and the confinement of the droplets were also studied .

test_26271|t|
test_26271|a|Physically reasonable results were obtained and provide insight into the conditions for coalescence .

test_26272|t|
test_26272|a|Simulations that match the conditions of experiments reported in the literature remain computationally impractical .
